chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: If the person in janabah immerses himself in water in a single immersion, that suffices him for his ghusl.

So this does not conflict with what we have previously stated regarding the obligation of sequence, because the one who immerses is considered sequential in legal judgment, even if he is not sequential in actual performance. For when he comes out of the water, it is judged first that his head has become pure, then his right side, then his left side, so on this basis it is considered ordered.
And it is possible that at the time of immersion, observing sequence is waived, just as in ghusl al-janabah the obligation of wudu is waived.

key_terms.ارْتِمَاسَةً: a full immersion of the body into water
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), whose obligation is discussed here
key_terms.حُكْمًا: in legal judgment or juridical consideration
key_terms.طَهَارَةِ: ritual purity attained through the act
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required for janabah
key_terms.وُجُوبِ التَّرْتِيبِ: the obligation of performing the washing in sequence

ai.seo_question: Does a single immersion in water suffice for ghusl al-janabah, and how is it reconciled with the requirement of sequence?
ai.summary: This report states that a single full-body immersion suffices for ghusl al-janabah. It also explains how this is reconciled with the requirement of sequence: either the order is recognized legally in judgment, or the requirement of sequence is waived in the case of immersion.
